children: By Bharath Rajeswaran and Jayshree P Upadhyay

India's equity benchmarks could see sharp swings in the final minutes of trade on Monday as MSCI-index linked investors adjust portfolios ahead of a rebalancing, providing the first major test of the new closing auction system.

The MSCI rejig takes effect on September 1, and funds tracking the index typically adjust their portfolios a day earlier to ensure they are aligned with the benchmark. With volumes in the new closing auction session still limited, the concentrated flows could trigger sharp price swings, traders said.

This MSCI rebalance is the first real litmus test for the CAS, said Arun Kejriwal, founder ​of Kejriwal Research and Investment Services. We could again see some "chaos" in individual stocks, he said.

Introduced on August 3, the CAS is a roughly 20-minute auction during which buy and sell orders are matched to determine a stock's official closing price. Similar mechanisms are used in other global and Asian markets, including China, Taiwan, Hong Kong and South Korea.
The system replaced a methodology under which closing prices were based on the average price of trades executed during the final 30 minutes of continuous trading.
The MSCI rejig adds four Indian companies: Laurus Labs
, Lenskart
, Adani Energy Solutions
and Groww
. They will replace Balkrishna Industries
, SBI Cards
, and Astral
The reshuffle with also reduce the weight for heavyweight Reliance Industries
and increase the weight for Adani Enterprises

"The larger names entering the MSCI basket are not major index components. Therefore, the volatility at the headline index level may not be very significant," said Tejas Shah, head of trading, Equirus Securities.
"The greater impact is likely to be stock-specific, with sharp moves possible in individual names depending on their liquidity and the scale of the passive flows."
SHARP SWINGS
The new closing auction has led to sharp swings, particularly on days when derivative contracts expire.

Last Thursday, the Sensex's indicative close pointed to a sharp 3.3% decline at one point during the closing auction session, which coincided with monthly derivatives expiry. The index later recovered to close 0.7% lower.

"MSCI rebalancing will bring its usual volatility. However, with no derivatives contracts expiring that day, even if closing auction results in some price distortion due to rebalancing flows, I expect its broader impact to remain limited," said Uttam Bagri, managing director, BCB Brokerage Private Limited.
